selection_rationale: cns-m2026-01 (GVR with reachability validator) is the strongest defensible, falsifiable, and venue-relevant study: it directly targets the operational reliability gap (intent→config safety), has a clear paired design and measurable primary outcome, and received a "pass" review while other candidates require substantive repairs (dataset/provenance, calibration, human-pilot conflicts).
unresolved_uncertainties: Extent of training-data contamination for public intent→config examples and its effect on baseline LLM success rates.
Deterministic reachability-validator false-negative rate relative to emulation/device execution (validator completeness limits).
Generalisability of emulation results (Mininet/container router images) to real device behavior and production topologies.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Implement provenance/audit procedures to detect and exclude examples likely present in LLM training data (dataset contamination controls).

Specify the exact reachability-validator implementation (e.g., Batfish-like engine), document known completeness/limitations, and add unit tests measuring validator false-negative rate against emulation.

Define and justify the emulation/testbed topology suite (Mininet/container images, router OS versions), isolate all execution to non-production testbeds, and document images/versions for reproducibility.
Preregister intent-normalization and ambiguity-resolution procedures (e.g., standardized intent schema, clarifying-question prompt policy, conservative interpretation rules).
Provide statistical power/sample-size justification for N (≥200), formalize the paired-test decision rule (e.g., McNemar/bootstrapped CI), and register the retry policy and random-seed protocol.
